payload.rationale: Dune: Part Three has been dated for December 18, 2026 by Warner Bros./Legendary since early 2025, principal photography reportedly completed in 2025, and by the September 2026 cutoff the film would be deep in post-production with marketing (trailers, IMAX commitments) underway. Tentpole releases three months out almost never slip; historical base rates for major studio films moving past their date within the final quarter, absent strikes or catastrophic events, are in the low single digits. The main disruptive factor is Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday also occupying December 18, 2026, which created speculation that one film would move; however, reports indicated WB held its date and Dune's IMAX screen commitments strengthened its position. If WB did move, an earlier date (which would not resolve YES) is at least as plausible as a later one. Reasons this estimate could be too high: the studio has repeatedly reaffirmed the date, the film is finished shooting, and a last-quarter move to 2027 would sacrifice awards-season and holiday positioning. Reasons it could be too low: the head-to-head clash with Avengers is unusual and could still prompt a late shuffle, VFX-heavy post-production can run late, and unforeseen events (industry labor actions, distribution disputes, or contractual settlement quirks such as limited early screenings versus wide release definitions) could technically trigger YES. No current research was supplied, so I cannot confirm the status as of September 2026; the estimate relies on background knowledge and base rates.
limitations: No supplied evidence; relies on general background knowledge with an information horizon that may predate the cutoff
Uncertain whether any date shuffle occurred between early 2026 and September 2026
Contract nuances (e.g., how early premieres or IMAX-only previews are treated) are not specified in the supplied text
